items.title: Long press a setting to clear it.
Dual Core (speedhack)
items.description: Split workload to two CPU cores instead of one. Increases speed.

items.title: CPU Boost
items.description: Keeps the CPU clocked up while a game runs (Ubuntu Touch has no game mode). Maximum doubled the speed of demanding games in testing.

items.title: Enable Savestates
items.description: WARNING: Savestates may not be compatible with future versions of Dolphin and can make it impossible to create normal saves in some cases. Never use savestates as the only way of saving your progress.

items.title: Use Panic Handlers
items.description: Show a message box when a potentially serious error has occurred. Disabling this may avoid annoying and non-fatal messages, but it may result in major crashes having no explanation at all.

items.title: Show On-Screen Display Messages
items.description: Display messages over the emulation screen area. These messages include memory card writes, video backend and CPU information, and JIT cache clearing.

items.title: Enable Play Time Tracking
items.description: Tracks the time you spend playing games and shows it in the game details.

items.title: Audio Buffer Size
items.description: Controls the number of audio samples buffered. Lower values reduce latency but may cause more crackling or stuttering. If unsure, set this to 80 ms.

items.title: Fill Audio Gaps
items.description: Repeat existing audio during lag spikes to prevent stuttering. If unsure, leave this checked.

items.title: Preserve Audio Pitch
items.description: Keeps audio at normal pitch when changing emulation speed. Without this, audio pitch changes proportionally with speed. If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: Skip Main Menu
items.description: Put IPL ROMs in User/GC/<region>

items.title: Widescreen
items.description: Changes aspect ratio from 4:3 to 16:9 in games that support it.

items.title: Use PAL60 Mode (EuRGB60)
items.description: Changes refresh rate from 50 Hz to 60 Hz in PAL games that support it.

items.title: Enable Screen Saver
items.description: Dims the screen after five minutes of inactivity.

items.title: Enable WiiConnect24 via WiiLink
items.description: Enables the WiiLink service for WiiConnect24 channels. Read the Terms of Service at https://www.wiilink24.com/tos

items.title: Insert SD Card
items.description: Supports SD and SDHC. Default size is 128 MB.

items.title: Automatically Sync with Folder
items.description: Synchronizes the SD Card with the SD Sync Folder when starting and ending emulation.

items.title: Pack SD Card Now
items.confirmation: You are about to pack the content of the SD sync folder into the SD card file. All current content of the file will be deleted. Are you sure you want to continue?

items.title: Unpack SD Card Now
items.confirmation: You are about to unpack the content of the SD card file into the SD sync folder. All current content of the folder will be deleted. Are you sure you want to continue?

items.title: Wii Remote Continuous Scanning
items.description: Leave this on if you are using a DolphinBar for real Wii Remote support.

items.title: Wii Remote Speaker
items.description: Enable sound output through the speaker on a real Wii Remote (DolphinBar required).

items.title: Enable MMU
items.description: Enables the Memory Management Unit. Needed for some games, but may reduce performance.

items.title: Pause on Panic
items.description: Pauses the emulation if a Read/Write or Unknown Instruction panic occurs. The performance impact is the same as having Enable MMU on.

items.title: Enable Write-Back Cache (slow)
items.description: Enables emulation of the CPU write-back cache. Enabling will have a significant impact on performance. This should be left disabled unless absolutely needed.

items.title: Override Emulated CPU Clock Speed
items.description: On games that have an unstable frame rate despite full emulation speed, higher values can improve their performance, requiring a powerful device. Lower values reduce the emulated console's performance, but improve the emulation speed.

items.title: Emulated CPU Clock Speed
items.description: Adjusts the emulated CPU's clock rate if "Override Emulated CPU Clock Speed" is enabled.

items.title: Override VBI Frequency
items.description: Makes games run at a different frame rate, making the emulation less demanding when lowered, or improving smoothness when increased. This may affect gameplay speed, as it is often tied to the frame rate.

items.title: VBI Frequency
items.description:
Adjusts the VBI frequency rate if "Override VBI Frequency" is enabled.
Also adjusts the emulated CPU's clock speed, to keep it relatively the same.

items.title: Enable Emulated Memory Size Override
items.description:
Sets the amount of RAM in the emulated console to the values provided.

WARNING: Enabling this will completely break many games. By default, Dolphin determines what value is required based on the game information.

items.title: Synchronize GPU Thread
items.description: Synchronizing the GPU thread reduces the risk of games crashing or becoming unstable with dual core enabled, but can also reduce the performance gain of dual core. If unsure, select "On Idle Skipping". Selecting "Never" is risky and not recommended!

items.title: Enable Custom RTC
items.description: This settings allows you to set a custom real time clock (RTC) separate from your current system time.

items.title: Emulate Disc Speed
items.description: Enable emulated disc speed. Disabling this can cause crashes and other problems in some games.

items.title: Compile Shaders Before Starting
items.description: This causes a delay when launching games, but will reduce stuttering early on.

items.title: Internal Resolution
items.description: Specifies the resolution used to render at. A high resolution will improve visual quality a lot but is also quite heavy on performance and might cause glitches in certain games.

items.title: Full-scene Anti-aliasing
items.description: Reduces the amount of aliasing caused by rasterizing 3D graphics. This makes the rendered picture look less blocky. Heavily decreases emulation speed and sometimes causes issues.

items.title: Anisotropic Filtering
items.description: Enhances visual quality of textures that are at oblique viewing angles. Might cause issues in a small number of games.

items.title: Texture Filtering
items.description: Overrides the texture scaling filter selected by the game. Any option except 'Default' will alter the look of the game's textures and might cause issues in a small number of games.

items.title: Scaled EFB Copy
items.description: Greatly increases quality of textures generated using render to texture effects. Raising the internal resolution will improve the effect of this setting. Slightly decreases performance and possibly causes issues (although unlikely).

items.title: Per-Pixel Lighting
items.description: Calculate lighting of 3D graphics per-pixel rather than per vertex. Decreases emulation speed by some percent (depending on your GPU). This usually is a safe enhancement, but might cause issues sometimes.

items.title: Force 24-Bit Color
items.description:
Forces the game to render the RGB color channels in 24-bit, thereby increasing quality by reducing color banding.
It has no impact on performance and causes few graphical issues. If unsure, leave this checked.

items.title: Disable Fog
items.description: Makes distant objects more visible by removing fog, thus increasing the overall detail. Disabling fog will break some games which rely on proper fog emulation.

items.title: Disable Copy Filter
items.description: Disables the blending of adjacent rows when copying the EFB. This is known in some games as "deflickering" or "smoothing". Disabling the filter is usually safe, and may result in a sharper image.

items.title: Arbitrary Mipmap Detection
items.description:
Enables detection of arbitrary mipmaps, which some games use for special distance-based effects.
May have false positives that result in blurry textures at increased internal resolution, such as in games that use very low resolution mipmaps. Disabling this can also reduce stutter in games that frequently load new textures.

If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: Widescreen Hack
items.description:
Forces the game to output graphics for any aspect ratio. Use with "Aspect Ratio" set to "Force 16:9" to force 4:3-only games to run at 16:9. Rarely produces good results and often partially breaks graphics and game UIs.
Unnecessary (and detrimental) if using any AR/Gecko-code widescreen patches. If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: Depth
items.description:
Control the distance between the virtual cameras.
A higher value creates a stronger feeling of depth while a lower value is more comfortable.

items.title: Convergence
items.description:
Control the distance of the convergence plane, this is the distance at which objects will appear to be in front of the screen.
A higher value creates stronger out-of-screen effects while a lower value is more comfortable.

items.title: Swap Eyes
items.description: Swap the left and right eye, mostly useful if you want to view side-by-side cross-eyed.

items.title: Skip EFB Access from CPU
items.description: Ignore any requests from the CPU to read/write to the EFB.

items.title: Ignore Format Changes
items.description: Ignore any changes to the EFB format.

items.title: Store EFB Copies to Texture Only
items.description: Stores EFB Copies exclusively on the GPU, bypassing system memory. Causes graphical defects in a small number of games. If unsure, leave this checked.

items.title: Defer EFB Copies to RAM
items.description: Waits until the game synchronizes with the emulated GPU before writing the contents of EFB copies to RAM. May result in faster performance. If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: Texture Cache Accuracy
items.description: The safer the selection, the less likely the emulator will be missing any texture updates from RAM.

items.title: GPU Texture Decoding
items.description: Decodes textures on the GPU using compute shaders where supported. May improve performance in some scenarios.

items.title: Store XFB Copies to Texture Only
items.description: Stores XFB Copies exclusively on the GPU, bypassing system memory. Causes graphical defects in a small number of games that need to readback from memory. If unsure, leave this checked.

items.title: Immediately Present XFB
items.description: Displays the XFB copies as soon as they are created, without waiting for scanout. Causes graphical defects in some games but reduces latency. If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: Skip Presenting Duplicate Frames
items.description: Skips presentation of duplicate frames. This may improve performance on low-end devices, while making frame pacing less consistent. If unsure, leave this checked.

items.title: Fast Depth Calculation
items.description: Uses a less accurate algorithm to calculate depth values. Causes issues in a few games, but can result in a decent speed increase depending on the game and/or GPU. If unsure, leave this checked.

items.title: Disable Bounding Box
items.description: Disables bounding box emulation. This may improve GPU performance significantly, but some games will break. If unsure, leave this checked.

items.title: Vertex Rounding
items.description: Rounds 2D vertices to whole pixels and rounds the viewport size to a whole number. Fixes graphical problems in some games at higher internal resolutions. This setting has no effect when native internal resolution is used. If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: VBI Skip
items.description: Skips Vertical Blank Interrupts when lag is detected, allowing for smooth audio playback when emulation speed is not 100%. Can cause freezes and compatibility issues.

items.title: Save Texture Cache to State
items.description: Includes the contents of the embedded frame buffer (EFB) and upscaled EFB copies in save states. Fixes missing and/or non-upscaled textures/objects when loading states at the cost of additional save/load time.

items.title: Show FPS
items.description: Shows the number of distinct frames rendered per second as a measure of visual smoothness.

items.title: Show Frame Times
items.description: Shows the average time in ms between each distinct rendered frame alongside the standard deviation.

items.title: Show VPS
items.description: Show the number of frames rendered per second as a measure of emulation speed.

items.title: Show VBlank Times
items.description: Shows the average time in ms between each rendered frame alongside the standard deviation.

items.title: Show Performance Graphs
items.description: Shows frametime graph along with statistics as a representation of emulation performance.

items.title: Show % Speed
items.description: Shows the % speed of emulation compared to full speed.

items.title: Show Speed Color
items.description: Changes the color of the FPS counter depending on emulation speed.

items.title: Log Render Time to File
items.description: Logs the render time of every frame to User/Logs/render_time.txt. Use this feature to measure Dolphin's performance.

items.title: Performance Sample Window
items.description: The amount of time the FPS and VPS counters will sample over. The higher the value, the more stable the FPS/VPS counter will be, but the slower it will be to update.

items.title: Graphics Mods
items.description: Loads graphics mods from User/Load/GraphicsMods/.

items.title: Load Custom Textures
items.description: Loads custom textures from User/Load/Textures/<game_id>/ and User/Load/DynamicInputTextures/<game_id>/.

items.title: Prefetch Custom Textures
items.description: Caches custom textures to system RAM on startup. This can require exponentially more RAM but fixes possible stuttering.

items.title: Dump Textures
items.description: Dumps decoded game textures based on the other flags to User/Dump/Textures/<game_id>/. If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: Dump Base Textures
items.description: Whether to dump base game textures to User/Dump/Textures/<game_id>/.

items.title: Dump Mip Maps
items.description: Whether to dump mipmapped game textures to User/Dump/Textures/<game_id>/.

items.title: To Aspect Ratio
items.description: Crops the picture from its native aspect ratio to 4:3 or 16:9. If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: Custom
items.description: Enables options to crop the picture by discrete native pixels (independent of the internal resolution setting) in order to attain a specific user target aspect ratio. Useful to resolve letterboxing issues. If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: Custom Top
items.description: Crops the picture top side by discrete native pixels (independent of the internal resolution setting) in order to attain a specific user target aspect ratio. If unsure, leave this value to 0.

items.title: Custom Bottom
items.description: Crops the picture bottom side by discrete native pixels (independent of the internal resolution setting) in order to attain a specific user target aspect ratio. If unsure, leave this value to 0.

items.title: Custom Left
items.description: Crops the picture left side by discrete native pixels (independent of the internal resolution setting) in order to attain a specific user target aspect ratio. If unsure, leave this value to 0.

items.title: Custom Right
items.description: Crops the picture right side by discrete native pixels (independent of the internal resolution setting) in order to attain a specific user target aspect ratio. If unsure, leave this value to 0.

items.title: V-Sync
items.description: This setting is unnecessary on most Android devices, because Android always enables V-Sync. If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: Backend Multithreading
items.description: Enables graphics backend multithreading (Vulkan only). May affect performance. If unsure, leave this checked.

items.title: Prefer VS for Point/Line Expansion
items.description: On backends that support both using the geometry shader and the vertex shader for expanding points and lines, selects the vertex shader for the job. May affect performance.

items.title: Cull Vertices on the CPU
items.description: Cull vertices on the CPU to reduce the number of draw calls required. May affect performance. If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: Defer EFB Cache Invalidation
items.description: Defers invalidation of the EFB access cache until a GPU synchronization command is executed. May improve performance in some games at the cost of stability. If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: Manual Texture Sampling
items.description: Use a manual implementation of texture sampling instead of the graphics backend's built-in functionality.

items.title: Dump Frames at Internal Resolution
items.description: Creates frame dumps and screenshots at the internal resolution of the renderer, rather than the size of the window it is displayed within. If the aspect ratio is widescreen, the output image will be scaled horizontally to preserve the vertical resolution.

items.title: Enable Wireframe
items.description: If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: Show Statistics
items.description: If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: Show Projection Statistics
items.description: If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: Show XFB Resolution
items.description: If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: Texture Format Overlay
items.description: If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: Enable API Validation Layers
items.description: If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: Dump EFB Target
items.description: If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: Dump XFB Target
items.description: If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: Disable EFB VRAM Copies
items.description: If unsure, leave this unchecked.

items.title: Write Logs to File
items.description: Log messages from enabled log types to the Logs folder. Will decrease performance.

items.confirmation: Are you sure you want to enable all log types?

items.confirmation: Are you sure you want to disable all log types?
